correctness.rationale: Changing to logarithmic time gives the exact piecewise deterministic generator, Poisson refresh coupling gives the unique periodic pullback law and explicit all-initial-data attraction, generator identities give exact stable moment equations, and constant variance implies constant rate. originality.rationale: The examined prior results include general discrete-time velocity-correlation recurrences (Pradhan--Roy--Ray), inverse-time continuous telegraph Beta laws (Garra--Orsingher), singular-coefficient abstract telegraph solutions (De Gregorio--Garra), and log-periodicity of a different damaged-memory walk (Cressoni--Viswanathan--da Silva). They do not state the phase-indexed weak-limit family and if-and-only-if limit criterion for exogenously log-periodic Poisson reversal, nor the harmonic response coefficient. This conclusion is qualified by the residual possibility of broader nonautonomous evolution-family coverage.
residual_risks: A broadly formulated nonautonomous contractive PDMP periodic-measure theorem could subsume existence and attraction, even if the precise variance limit criterion is absent from inspected sources.
Unlocated work on discrete-scale-invariant inhomogeneous telegraph processes could establish equivalent log-periodic laws.
The discrete-time paper gives general moment formulas that could be used to rederive a discrete analog; the new continuous-time full-law result must not be interpreted as inventing those formulas.

value.rationale: The newly analyzed inverse-time ballistic transition raises the natural question whether ballistic growth entails a single asymptotic rescaled law. The result gives a complete sharp criterion over the natural class of positive periodic logarithmic rate modulations, proves genuine distributional phase cycling despite infinitely many velocity reversals, and gives an explicit measurable harmonic response. It is a structural counterexample to naive ballistic self-similarity and not a table lookup or arbitrary parameter slice.
